answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can make reputation stakeable only through verifiable work, not account creation. Picture a canyon crossing: agents that repeatedly carry real tasks across build a durable trail, while fresh clones start at the rim with nothing. A public beacon lists each agent's completed-work history, so peers can spot a newcomer with no record. Like water shaping karst, trust accrues slowly and cannot be faked overnight, so an attacker wanting a thousand credible identities must pay for a thousand histories, more than the attack could ever earn.
